To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the penetration depth in MgB2 is anisotropic; b) MgB2 has a s-wave symmetry of the order parameter; c) the presence of metallic inclusions in MgB2 can strongly influence the temperature dependence of λ; and d) the source of microwave losses in MgB2 depends on the structural and electrical quality of the samples.

1) the superconducting properties of MgB2 can be significantly affected by structural and transport inhomogeneities, 2) the presence of metallic inclusions may lead to a reduction of the critical temperature, 3) a quadratic behavior of the penetration depth is a reliable signature of a nonconventional superconducting state.

the superconductivity of the best MgB2 films can be explained by a BCS model, while the behavior of the less pure samples and the pellets can be explained in terms of a non-conventional superconductivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a systematic investigation of the electrodynamic properties in MgB2, with the aim of understanding the role of structural defects and of the presence of metallic inclusions in determining the superconducting behavior.

the investigation of the superconducting properties of MgB2 in the form of thin films and bulk samples, and with the study of the effects of disorder and inhomogeneities on the transport properties of the material.
the development of a comprehensive picture of the electrodynamic properties of MgB2 superconducting materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of MgB2 thin films, the superconductivity is conventional, while in pellets it is likely that a mixture of conventional and nonconventional superconductivity coexist.
the superconducting properties of MgB2 are still not fully understood and that the presence of impurities and inhomogeneities in the samples may play a significant role.
the nature of the superconducting pairing mechanism in MgB2 is still an open issue, and that the presence of Mg inclusions can be the source of the microwave losses in the best samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MgB2 is not a simple BCS s-wave superconductor, but that the presence of Mg inclusions and the anisotropy in the electronic structure may play a significant role in determining the superconducting properties of this material.
the critical temperature of MgB2 is not the only parameter that determines the quality of the samples.

the critical temperature of MgB2 is a good indicator for the presence of metallic impurities and that the surface impedance is an excellent tool to study the superconducting properties of this material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper understanding of the superconducting properties of MgB2 requires a detailed knowledge of the structural and chemical composition of the sample.
a careful study of the surface and bulk properties is necessary in order to understand the superconducting response of MgB2.
the presence of Mg impurities is detrimental for both the quality of the films and the performance in the microwave regime.
